- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., < 0.33) and supply net is large negative, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 30d mean), model often overshoots and fails to revert — apply mean reversion bias toward prior 10-15d average.
- If official event count is high and bearish sentiment dominates, model underestimates downside risk — increase downward bias or add 3-5% floor adjustment.
- When sentiment is mixed (e.g., 0.33–0.67) and supply net is negative, model often fails to capture volatility — add 1-2% volatility buffer to forecast range.
- If model forecast is flat or rising slowly but true outcome shows sharp decline, model is lagging — adjust for recent event momentum (e.g., if 3 events in 3d, forecast should drop 2-3% per event).
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is bullish but supply net is negative, model often overestimates recovery — reduce forecast by 1-2% for each bearish event in last 7d.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed and true outcome shows strong mean reversion, model tends to overpredict trend — apply 1-3% downward correction if price > 1.5x prior 30d mean.
